Guide

Turn a YouTube video into text

Verbi turns the speech in a YouTube video into text: paste the video’s link into the app, and Verbi transcribes the audio in any of 39 languages, ready to read, search, copy and summarize, and with Pro to export. Verbi is an AI note taker for iPhone and Android that’s free to start, with 60 minutes of transcription a month; on the free plan, the app shows any limit that applies to video imports.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Last updated: November 16, 2026

How do I transcribe a YouTube video?

  1. Copy the video’s link in YouTube: tap Share, then Copy link.
  2. Open Verbi, tap Load from YouTube and paste the link.
  3. Tap Import Video. Verbi fetches the audio from the video and transcribes it, so you don’t need to download anything yourself.
  4. Read the transcript, search it or copy it. With Pro, you can also export it as TXT or PDF.
  5. For the gist, generate a summary with a template such as Lesson Notes or Blog Post, or with Pro ask the transcript a question.

What can I do with a video transcript?

  • Read a talk or a tutorial instead of watching it, and find it again later by searching for anything that was said.
  • With Pro, turn a recorded class into lesson notes that stick to what was said in the video.
  • With Pro, ask questions like “What were the three steps she recommended?” and get answers drawn from the video’s words.
  • Translate the transcript into English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Indonesian, Dutch, Polish or Simplified Chinese (Pro).
  • Copy a quote or the whole text, or with Pro export it as TXT or PDF.

Which videos can I transcribe?

  • Verbi works with YouTube links: regular videos, Shorts and youtu.be links.
  • The video needs speech. Music or footage without talking gives you little or no text.
  • For a recording that isn’t on YouTube, import the audio file, or share it to Verbi from another app.
  • Transcribe videos you’re entitled to use, such as your own uploads or public talks for your own notes, and respect the creator’s rights when you share the text.

Is video to text free?

Verbi is free to download. The free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription a month, recordings kept for 15 days and 3 AI summaries a month. On the free plan, a video counts toward those 60 minutes and has to fit in the minutes you have left, and the app shows any other limit on video imports when it applies.

Verbi Pro takes longer videos and more imports, and adds hours of transcription (20 a month, or 5 a week on the weekly plan; MAX doubles that), an AI summary for every transcript, translation, chat with the transcript, export and recordings kept past 15 days. Transcripts are stored on your phone. To import a video, our server fetches its audio from YouTube and deletes its copy automatically; the privacy policy has the details.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to download the video first?

No. Paste the link and Verbi fetches the audio itself. Nothing needs to be saved to your phone first.

Does it work with videos in other languages?

Yes. Verbi transcribes 39 languages and can detect the language on its own. With Pro, you can translate the transcript into English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Indonesian, Dutch, Polish or Simplified Chinese.

Is there a limit on video length?

On the free plan, a video has to fit in the minutes you have left this month, and the app shows any other limit when it applies. Verbi Pro takes longer videos and more imports, within your plan’s hours.
